subject: Latency spike after qprofile v2 rollout - urgent
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@falconpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@falconpay.com>, CTO Ops <cto.ops@falconpay.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual p99 spike since qprofile v2 rolled (prod)

Hi Vivek,

We rolled the qprofile v2 that Redwood recommended last night (11/23) during our low traffic window. Since the rollout, we're seeing a sustained p99 increase from ~350ms to ~890ms on the hot inference path for authorization scoring. Error rate climbed to 0.9% (5xx) for short-lived bursts. This is materially impacting user flows for payments.

I've attached a small perf trace and a dashboard snapshot. Can your team confirm whether the model variant or execution path changed and advise an immediate mitigation? Our customer ops and CTO are already looped in.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Platform Reliability, FalconPay
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@falconpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual p99 spike since qprofile v2 rolled (prod)

Samir — thanks for the quick note and the traces. We see the same signal in our telemetry. Apologies for the disruption; we'll treat this as high priority.

Immediate next steps:
- Irene: can you take lead on root cause (kernel path vs qprofile mismatch)?
- Priyom: prepare a rollback plan for qprofile v1 and a controlled throttle on requests to the affected model route.
- Lauren: I'll coordinate the exec comms and share an ETA with FalconPay leadership.

Samir — we'll follow up within 45 minutes with a preliminary diagnosis and the rollback window if needed.

Regards,
Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual p99 spike since qprofile v2 rolled (prod)

Quick update from infra:
- Reproduced the p99 regression on a canary with identical traffic distribution.
- Trace shows a fallback to a float32 execution kernel for batches >128 due to an unexpected pad alignment on V100 nodes; this path increases compute and GC churn for the model runtime.
- qprofile-v2 enabled an aggressive group-quant path that changes the batching breakpoint; that combined with our kernel selection heuristic pushed some tokens into the slower path.

Attached quick perf dump. My recommendation: rollback to qprofile-v1 for the FalconPay route and schedule a qprofile-v2 variant with a conservative batching threshold. Priyom, please prepare the rollback runbook.

Irene
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@falconpay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual p99 spike since qprofile v2 rolled (prod)

Samir — proposed rollback plan below (minimal blast radius):
1) Schedule rollback window: 11/24 17:30 - 17:45 PT.
2) Execute rollback of qprofile v2 -> v1 on FalconPay model route (single-region).
3) Monitor p50/p95/p99, error rate, and token throughput for 30 minutes post-rollback.
4) If metrics return to baseline, leave v1 and gate v2 with a conservative batch threshold in a canary for 48 hours.

If FalconPay prefers an immediate rollback, we can move earlier — we'd need a 15-minute coordination call to confirm traffic drain and active connection handoff.

Attachments: rollout-runbook-rollback.txt (runbook stub)

— Priyom
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@falconpay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@falconpay.com>, CTO Ops <cto.ops@falconpay.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual p99 spike since qprofile v2 rolled (prod)

Samir / Elena — follow-up from today's operations:

We executed the rollback to qprofile-v1 at 17:33 PT on 11/24 per the runbook. Observed results:
- p99 dropped from ~890ms to ~360ms within 8 minutes.
- Error rate fell from 0.9% to 0.08%.
- Throughput returned to baseline; no token loss observed.

Root cause (summary): an interaction between qprofile-v2's batching breakpoint and our kernel-selection heuristic led to unexpected float32 fallback for large batches on certain V100 firmware revisions. This increased per-token compute and occasional GC pauses in the runtime.

Action items:
- Short term: keep FalconPay on qprofile-v1. We will ship a patched kernel-selection heuristic and a v2 variant that enforces a lower batch threshold within 72 hours.
- Medium term: add a preflight synthetic that validates kernel selection across hardware/firmware permutations before qprofile rollout.
- Exec comms: Lauren will prepare a brief for FalconPay leadership summarizing impact, timelines, and compensation options (we discussed a service credit).

Samir — apologies again. We prioritized rollback to stop user impact. We'll share the patched rollout plan tomorrow and are available for a call with your CTO.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
